name: TPx Communications

profile.address: 2001, East Dyer Road, Dyer, Santa Ana, Orange County, California, 92705
profile.reading:
This Santa Ana building at 2001 East Dyer Road, in Orange County's Dyer industrial district near John Wayne Airport, houses a colocation and managed services data center operated by TPx Communications. TPx traces its roots to 1998, when it launched in California as a competitive local exchange carrier, one of many companies that emerged after federal telecommunications deregulation opened local phone markets to competitors of the regional Bell operating companies. Over the following two decades the company grew and consolidated through a series of mergers, most notably with US TelePacific, and repositioned itself from a pure telecom carrier into a nationwide managed IT services provider spanning managed IT support, cybersecurity, business connectivity, and unified communications.

The Santa Ana facility is marketed under TPx's MSx Datacenters line, which the company describes as offering multiple layers of infrastructure redundancy in a parallel and protected configuration, with power delivered in standard 120 and 208 volt configurations to customer cabinets and cages ranging from partial cabinet space up to full private suites. TPx states the site operates under an SSAE 18 service organization control examination, the standard third party audit framework used to evaluate a service provider's internal controls, and that it supports customers with HIPAA and PCI compliance obligations who need to house regulated data outside their own offices. Connectivity is advertised with network availability of 99.999 percent across redundant fiber paths, and bandwidth packages from a few megabits per second up to gigabit speeds.

As is typical of a carrier owned colocation site rather than a hyperscale or wholesale campus, TPx has not published square footage, total power capacity, or a build date for the Santa Ana building specifically, and the company does not appear in county assessor or permit records under a name that ties those filings unambiguously to a data center use. What is publicly confirmed is that TPx operates and staffs the site, offers a 24 hour remote hands support line reachable through a dedicated Santa Ana option on its national hotline, and positions the facility as one node in a broader footprint of regional colocation and network points of presence it uses to serve small and mid sized business customers across the markets it grew into from its original Southern California telecom base.

reading:
TPx Communications is a managed IT services and telecommunications provider, headquartered in Austin, that began life in 1998 as TelePacific Communications, a California competitive local exchange carrier. It grew by acquisition through the 2010s, took the TPx name in April 2017, and was acquired by Siris Capital Group in a transaction cleared by the FCC in 2019 and 2020. Its regulated entities still file as a family, and an FCC compliance filing made on 1 May 2026 covering calendar year 2025 lists them: U.S. TelePacific Corp., Mpower Communications Corp., Arrival Communications, Inc., DSCI, LLC and TPx Communications Co.

TPx is in a data centre registry because it operates colocation space for its own network customers rather than because it builds wholesale halls. Its own MSx Datacenters product description is candid about the scale. Space is sold as a third of a cabinet, a half cabinet, a full cabinet or a cage. Cabinets are 30 inches wide and 36 inches deep, half height at 42 inches and full height at 84 inches, adjustable to 19 or 23 inch rails and braced for seismic zone 4. Power is quoted as receptacles, 120 volt at 20 or 30 amps and 208 volt at 20 or 30 amps, with special options on request. The sites use standard commercial utility power as the primary source with back-up generators behind it, protected power delivered through an inverter or UPS at some locations, FM-200 fire suppression with VESDA monitored pre-action detection, and an SSAE 18 audit. TPx states plainly that its facilities are not carrier neutral, being provided for its own network customers, though other providers are permitted to deliver circuits at some sites. Nowhere does the company publish an IT load, a utility service size or a generator rating, and the deepest power figure it discloses is a receptacle amperage.

The registry's single row is 2001 East Dyer Road in Santa Ana, one of two sites TPx names in its remote hands hotline menu alongside Sacramento. The building is a commercial structure of roughly 36,900 square feet in footprint and about 8.6 metres tall, and Orange County addressing places the TPx space at unit 102 within it. The provenance of the record deserves noting. The outline was drawn in May 2017 as a plain commercial building and named TPx Colocation Datacenter that November. It did not acquire a data centre classification until 29 June 2025, and the operator name and an alternate name were only added on 9 December 2025, in an edit whose own source tag cites two commercial data centre directories. In other words, the classification in this registry descends from directory listings rather than from a permit, a filing or the operator.

One point remains unresolved. Press coverage reported that TPx filed for Chapter 11 protection in June 2026, and that report has not been confirmed here against a court docket or a company statement. What the regulatory record does show is that the carrier entities remained licensed through 2026 and that counsel filed a pro forma notification on 16 July 2026 in FCC docket 19-248, the docket covering transfer of control of U.S. TelePacific Holdings. A pro forma filing of that kind is consistent with an internal ownership restructuring, and the corporate status of this operator should be rechecked before the Santa Ana row is relied on.
